answers.how: The ball trajectory gives downward acceleration ≈1665 px/s², so the scale is 9.8/1665 ≈0.00589 m/px. Its diameter is ≈41 px.
A single wall pad is ≈96.8 px wide. Using the gravity-derived scale of ≈0.00589 m/px gives ≈57 cm.
The pads extend ≈282 px vertically; multiplying by the gravity-derived scale gives ≈166 cm.
At 1.50 s, the ball's lower edge is at ≈156 px and the local floor level is ≈385 px. The ≈229 px bottom-to-floor gap converts to ≈1.35 m.
The ball center moves from ≈(86,209) px to ≈(608,211) px, a displacement magnitude of ≈522 px. Converted using the gravity-derived scale.
Near 1.50 s, horizontal velocity is ≈860 px/s and vertical velocity is nearly zero. The resulting speed converts to ≈5.06 m/s.
The person's full height is approximately 314 px across the upright walking frames. Converted using ≈0.00589 m/px.
Tracking the person's torso from 2.50 s to 3.50 s gives ≈246 px of horizontal travel in 1.00 s. Converted using the gravity-derived scale.
